v.text: Calgary once had no wards at all.
v.said: Calgary once had no wards at all.

v.text: When it became a city in eighteen ninety-four, it had three wards, with three aldermen each.
v.said: When it became a city in eighteen ninety-four, it had three wards, with three aldermen each.

v.text: Then, from nineteen fourteen, wards were dropped. For almost fifty years, every alderman was elected by the whole city.

v.text: In nineteen sixty, voters chose to bring them back: six wards, with two aldermen each.

v.text: The nineteen seventy-seven election was the first with fourteen wards, one alderman each.

v.text: And the lines keep moving. As the city grows, wards are redrawn to keep about the same number of voters in each.
